key_facts: Patient is a teenage girl from Saint-Martin
Presented with bilateral blurred vision and ocular irritation
Experienced fever and severe arthralgia one month earlier
Ocular history is negative for trauma and previous inflammation
Primary HIV infection, tuberculosis, sarcoidosis, and syphilis have been ruled out
Slitlamp biomicroscopy revealed bilateral punctate superficial keratitis and stromal immune ring formation
Aqueous tap PCR results are positive for Chikungunya virus with weak viral load
IgM CHIKV serologic test is positive

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including bilateral blurred vision and ocular irritation, along with the presence of Chikungunya virus in the aqueous tap PCR results and positive IgM CHIKV serologic test, strongly suggest an ocular infection caused by the Chikungunya virus.

rejected.label: Chikungunya virus infection
rejected.why: While the patient has a Chikungunya virus infection, this option is too broad and does not specifically address the ocular symptoms.

rejected.label: Uveitis
rejected.why: Although the patient presents with some signs of uveitis, such as stromal immune ring formation and keratic precipitates, the specific cause of these symptoms is identified as Chikungunya virus ocular infection.
